name: Two roads to a graph convolution
title: Spectral and spatial: two roads to a graph convolution
blurb: Convolution cannot be lifted from a grid onto a graph unchanged, so the field built it twice. One road reads the Laplacian's eigenvectors as the graph's Fourier basis and defines convolution there; the other writes the aggregation directly on vertices and relations. This section walks the spectral road — the eigenbasis, the convolution, the two problems that stalled it, and the polynomial approximation that rescued it — and then places the paper's own incidence-matrix layer on the spatial road.
